Where it began

Dhruv Jurel, born on 21 January 2001, grew up in Agra. Cricket found him at a school summer camp, where he saw a game going on and wanted to join in. He soon left home to train at an academy in Noida, on the edge of Delhi, and worked his way through Uttar Pradesh's under-14, under-16 and under-19 sides.

He was vice-captain of India at the 2020 Under-19 World Cup, and two years later he made his first-class debut for Uttar Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy.

The player

He bats right-handed and keeps wicket. His first Test call came in January 2024, and he made his debut against England at Rajkot that February, scoring 46 in his only innings. In the next Test, at Ranchi, he made 90 in the first innings while wickets fell at the other end, then came back with an unbeaten 39 in the second, sharing a stand of 72 with Shubman Gill and hitting the winning runs. It was his second Test, it made the series India's, and he was named player of the match.

In 2025 he kept wicket as a substitute in England when Rishabh Pant was hurt. Later, against Sri Lanka, he made an unbeaten 115, his first Test hundred away from home. By November 2026 he had played 12 Tests and made 651 runs at 40.69, with 2 hundreds, a best of 125, and 13 catches and 2 stumpings behind the stumps.

What made him special

At Ranchi, with England on top and wickets falling around him, he batted with the patience of a much older player, and he did it again in the second innings to see India home. That knack of staying calm when the match is tight was the mark of his first years in the side.

By November 2026 he had bowled in Tests without taking a wicket. The gloves look like the safer bet.

Away from the middle

Rajasthan Royals bought him in the 2022 auction, and on his first appearance for them, against Punjab Kings at Guwahati in 2023, he hit 32 not out from 15 balls, which settled his place in the side. In August 2025 he was named captain of Central Zone for the Duleep Trophy.

And finally

Most players spend a few Tests finding their feet. Jurel used his second one to win a series, which rather raised the bar for everyone else's second Test.
